correctness.rationale: The unselected (i,j) has exactly r_i+c_j selected neighbors, so feasibility iff r_i+c_j>=2. Every column occupied forces >=n; any empty column forces all m row degrees >=2 and >=2m. Explicit feasible constructions achieve min(n,2m); equality forces precisely surjective singleton columns or degree-two rows. The n=2m intersection is 2-regular rows and one-per-column, counted (2m)!/2^m, proving the counting formula incl. m=n=1. A separately written neighborhood brute force over all 10 m<=n<=4 matrices exactly reproduced size and counts (e.g. 44 at (2,4)). This finite check corroborates but is not the universal proof.
